title: Re-evaluation of Growth Hormone Deficiency in Adolescence: A Longitudinal Analysis from 2010 to 2025
summary:
Growth hormone deficiency (GHD) is one of the most commonly diagnosed endocrine disorders in childhood and adolescence, leading, among other things, to a significant impairment of height growth. During adolescence and the subsequent transitional phase—the period between the end of linear growth and the attainment of full adult maturity—growth hormone also plays a crucial role in building peak bone mass and optimizing body composition by promoting lean body mass and reducing visceral fat.
Clinical practice, however, faces the challenge that a significant proportion of patients diagnosed with isolated GHD in childhood show normal GH secretion upon re-evaluation after growth has ceased. Identifying and distinguishing patients with persistent growth hormone deficiency in adolescence is therefore crucial, both to ensure long-term health in cases of persistent deficiency and to minimize the costs and risks associated with lifelong therapy.

The primary objective of this retrospective study is to analyze the clinical and diagnostic parameters in patients with GHD from the time of initial diagnosis through re-evaluation during adolescence. Three specific aspects will be evaluated: the assessment of treatment effects on anthropometry, the frequency and identification of predictors for the persistence of the deficiency, and the validation of the arginine test as a diagnostic tool in comparison to the insulin tolerance test.

interventions.name:
Since this is a retrospective, single-center confirmatory study, all available data sets from patients who were treated for growth hormone deficiency (GHD) between 2010 and 2025 and re-evaluated during adolescence using the arginine test and the insulin tolerance test are included.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Since this is a retrospective, single-center confirmatory study, all available data sets from patients who were treated for growth hormone deficiency (GHD) between 2010 and 2025 and re-evaluated at our center using arginine and insulin tolerance tests will be included.
Exclusion criteria:
- Discontinued growth hormone therapy
- Incomplete testing
